2. The plaintiff-petitioners' case, in short, is that the land under the plaint schedule comprising an area of 1.10 acres being khas land admittediy belonged to Bangladesh Government and the plaintiffs are stranded persons from India and being the landless persons settled in the suit land 46 years before with permission from the then government authority. They removed jungle from the said land and converted it into cultivable and homestead land and started to live there. Later by permanent Settlement Case No.174 of 91-92, Bangladesh Government permanently entitled settlement of the plaintiff-respondent petitioners in the same land through a registered Kabuliyat dated 22-8-1991. The plaintiff petitioners mutated the suit land and also paid the rent as usual to the Government. At the instance of present high price of the land in the area due to establishment of India-Bangladesh Export-Import Station nearby the government officials being instigated by interested quarters without acknowledging the plaintiff-petitioners cancelled the permanent lease settlement on 26-4-2001 under the signature of defendant No.4 without serving any prior notice to the plaintiff petitioners and trying to make lease of the said land to third parties collusively. Consequently the plaintiff-petitioners are not bound by the illegal cancellation of the lease deed. Admittedly, there are dwelling houses of the plaintiff-petitioners over the suit land and in spite of that the defendant-opposite parties are trying to lease out the suit land to the third parties and hence the case. 

 5. On the reverse, the learned Advocate for the plaintiff-petitioners argued that the defendants executed a registered kabuliyat with the plaintiff-petitioners and only a civil court can cancel a registered document and a simple resolution by a committee is not at all enough to cancel a lease deed which is a registered document. Moreover cancellation of lease without prior notice and without giving opportunity for hearing such cancellation is contrary to natural justice. Admittedly the defendants leased out the suit land in the name of the plaintiff-petitioners who are in possession of the suit land and government failed to submit any copy of gazette notification to prove that the suit land is reserve forest and thus plaintiff-petitioners deserve relief in the suit. 

 6. The trial court examined 2 witnesses from the plaintiff-petitioners' side and also examined 1 witness from the defend ant-opposite parties. The plaintiff-petitioners exhibited before the court the registered kabuliyat which was executed between Bangladesh Government and the plaintiff-petitioners and that the said kabuliyat was registered upon a proceeding of the government office. The plaintiff-petitioners also exhibited the mutated khatian against the suit land in their names and rent receipts of the said land were also produced before the learned court. 

 8. During trial, the plaintiff-petitioners proved their case by deposition of witnesses, by exhibits of registered kabuliyat, evidences of payment of rents to the government and suit khatian before the court. 

 11. Learned Advocates Mr. M Khaled Ahmed along with Mr. Md. Siddiqur Rahman appearing on behalf of the petitioners at the very outset submitted that the plaintiff-petitioners got the deed by way of executing kabuliyat and enjoying the property. According to condition they are enjoying the property for last 40 years. Initially the land was in full of jungle and not inhabitable. Then they removed jungle from the suit land and converted it into cultivable and homestead land and started to live there. He further submits that now the value of the suit land has increased remarkably and some ill motivated persons and land grabber tried to grab the land and filed an application before the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet for cancellation of the lease and to use the land themselves. Accordingly the Upazila Nirbahi Officer, Goainghat, Sylhet submitted a report and considering the same the Deputy Commissioner cancelled the lease and directed to evict them from the leased out land, that is, cause of filing of the suit for declaration of title and permanent injunction. 

 12. In the trial court the plaintiff-petitioners examined two witnesses and submitted their relevant documents before the court which are marked as exhibits. The trial court upon perusing the records mainly the kabuliyat and rent receipts delivered the judgment in the terms as quoted herein below:— 

 13. Against the judgment of the trial court the Government filed appeal being Title Appeal No.176 of 2011. The main contention in the appeal is that the land was awarded to the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners by executing kabuliyat and it is admitted position that the land owned by the Government and considering the leasee they were migrated from India to Bangladesh. For their rehabilitation the Government allotted the entire land for their use and constructing the house so that they can live with others. The Government filed appeal and it is contended that the lease violated the condition of lease, that is, the kabuliyat, condition No.21 which is quoted herein below by the appellate court. 

 16. On the other hand learned Deputy Attorney-General Abdul Wahab along with Ms. Shahana Parveen and Sanda Ghosh appearing on behalf of the opposite parties-Government very outset forcefully submitted that this Rule should be discharged on the ground that the kabuliyat executed in favour of the plaintiff-respondent-petitioners they have violated the conditions binding upon them. It is stated in the kabuliyat that if they violate any condition the deed will be cancelled. He read out the judgment of the appellate court and submits that there are 22 conditions, out of which they have violated the condition Nos.8 and 21. The condition No.21 has been quoted in the judgment of the appellate court and the condition No.8 is, without cultivating the leasee will not use the land for other purpose. But if the leasee has no land for living, in that case with written permission of the Deputy Commissioner he can use 008 acre of land as homestead. 

 22. It is unfortunate for the appellate court who delivered the judgment without following the judgment of the Hon'ble Appellate Division and it is quite natural to serve notice to the lease who is enjoying the property by way of kabuliyat for long 40 years. They have family members and existence of everything. But the Deputy Commissioner, Sylhet falling in misconception of law and become biased by the influential person and land grabbers initiated proceeding for cancellation of lease and ultimately he cancelled.
